messages:
carmen: Quick edge-case - we have an internal transfer whose official hire/transfer date is 12/31 but in their local timezone that's 11:30pm. Payroll cutoff for their legal entity is 12/30. Will they be eligible for year-end carryover and company shutdown pay?
lee: Two parts: carryover depends on being active on payroll on Dec 31 for that legal entity. If payroll cutoff is 12/30 and they aren’t tagged by then, payroll won't mark them as active for 12/31. Shutdown pay also follows payroll tagging rules.
sanjay: Also note transfer vs new hire: sometimes transfers generate retro pay tags if paperwork is processed late, but we can't rely on that for carryover eligibility unless People Ops requests an exception.
hr-bot: POLICY CLIP: "Eligibility for carryover: employee must be on payroll as of Dec 31 in their employing entity. Company shutdown holiday pay is applied to employees active on the shutdown start date per payroll records. Exceptions require People Ops approval and payroll tagging prior to the run cutoff."
carmen: Okay - manager is panicking because the transfer was coordinated late and the person will be performing in the new role during the shutdown. Manager wants them to receive shutdown pay and be eligible for carryover. Any fast-route?
lee: Fast-route: if all onboarding paperwork is complete, People Ops can submit a payroll ticket to force an "active-on-Dec31" tag for that employee. Payroll needs confirmation and the ticket before the payroll cutoff (12/30 in this case). Otherwise we'd need a manual adjustment in January which is slower and can complicate carryover automation.
sanjay: If payroll can't tag retroactively in time, People Ops can approve a one-time manual carryover grant post-payroll, but we require manager justification and legal notice. That will be a manual journal entry.
carmen: How about sick-top-up or onboarding credit? Could we grant a one-time 4-day sick credit instead of messing with payroll tagging for shutdown pay?
lee: Yes, short-term solution: approve a one-time sick credit (one-time paycode) that payroll can add next cycle. That doesn't change carryover status though. If manager needs carryover eligibility too, either payroll tag before cutoff or a manual carryover grant later.
hr-bot: SUGGESTED WORKFLOW: 1) Manager confirms in writing and attaches completed paperwork. 2) People Ops opens payroll ticket with "active-on-dec31" request before cutoff, or requests manual carryover grant post-run with justification. 3) For immediate coverage, People Ops may approve a one-time sick/top-up credit; payroll will apply on next pay cycle if tagged by Jan 7.
sanjay: Also alert: for transfers that change employing entity (e.g., US -> UK), carryover caps and holiday rules may differ by country; double-check local policy.
carmen: Got it. I'll ask the manager to upload documents now and choose: (A) try payroll tag before cutoff, or (B) accept manual adjustment + one-time sick credit.
lee: If you pick A, cc payroll early. If B, include business justification and confirm requested carryover days (<= cap).
carmen: Will do. One more question: if we approve manual carryover after payroll, does that show in benefits portal automatically?
sanjay: After manual adjustment it shows as an off-cycle credit and should sync, but sometimes benefits portal needs a refresh; payroll will include a note in the comment. Expect a 1-2 pay-cycle lag.
carmen: Perfect. I'll update the manager and follow up with the ticket. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
